subject: Request: temporary streaming delivery-pattern exception for Q4 load test
messages:
From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@bluepeak.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@bluepeak.com
Date: 2026-08-04T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Q4 load test — request for temporary streaming delivery-pattern exception

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We are lining up a high-fidelity load test for late September to validate our product's embed-and-chat pipeline. The test will spike sustained request rates in 10–15 minute bursts (simulating batch ingestion + chat fan-out).

Two asks:
- Can Redwood designate a temporary SLA carveout for streaming endpoints during the test window (Sept 20–Sept 24)? Specifically: time-to-first-token (TTFT) expectations of 300ms at P95 instead of your standard 120ms during those bursts, and a reduced sustained tokens/sec commitment for the streaming tier so our load doesn't trigger immediate throttling policies.
- If a carveout isn't feasible, can you confirm the best alternative: dedicated capacity or routing to a non-streaming bulk endpoint that guarantees throughput but with higher TTFT?

Attached is our Q4 load plan with expected RPS and token distributions. We want to finalize this in the next two weeks so contracting can align.

Thanks — Evan
Evan Liu
Head of Platform, BluePeak Analytics
attachments: bluepeak-q4-load-plan.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@bluepeak.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 load test — request for temporary streaming delivery-pattern exception

Evan — thanks for the detail and the attachment. I looped in Karthik (sales engineering) and Sean (SRE) to evaluate. Quick thoughts:

- We can consider a temporary exception but need to validate impact on existing customers sharing pooled capacity.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) is the cleanest approach for predictable throughput; it avoids SLA carveouts that could affect multitenant guarantees.
- If you prefer to stay on hosted streaming, we could offer a controlled policy: during the test window Redwood applies a permissive rate policy for BluePeak, with a documented TTFT expectation of P95 <= 300ms for bursts and explicit throttling thresholds beyond sustained token/sec X (we need to size X together). This would be a signed exception and limit scope to the test window.

Action items for us: Sean will run a quick capacity impact analysis and propose token/sec ceilings. Karthik — can you prepare the temporary carveout terms for contracts? Evan — can you confirm exact burst patterns (per-minute RPS + token distribution) so we can model?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: requested-slo-carveout-form.pdf
From: k arthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Evan Liu <evan.liu@bluepeak.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 load test — request for temporary streaming delivery-pattern exception

Thanks Marissa — adding a few contractual guardrails we typically use for temporary carveouts so the legal team has language ready:

1) Scope: exception applies only to the BluePeak account and only within the agreed test window (dates inclusive).
2) SLAs modified: TTFT P95 <= 300ms during burst windows; sustained token/sec commitment lowered to a negotiated gross rate (e.g., 250k tokens/min) for the streaming tier. Non-streaming bulk endpoints retain separate throughput and cost profiles.
3) Isolation: Redwood will attempt to provision soft isolation (tagged scheduling/pools) but cannot guarantee full single-tenant isolation without dedicated capacity.
4) Metrics & rollback: exception is conditional on no measurable degradation to other customers. Redwood reserves the right to enforce limits or switch traffic to a non-streaming fallback if cross-tenant impact exceeds thresholds.

I can draft a one-page amendment and share with contracts@bluepeak.com for signature. Evan — happy to include a short acceptance checklist (capacity model + expected token curves).

—Karthik
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Evan Liu <evan.liu@bluepeak.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 load test — request for temporary streaming delivery-pattern exception

Evan / team — I ran a preliminary impact simulation (linked below). Key findings:
- Given BluePeak's projected burst profile (peaks ~1.8x normalized baseline for 12–18 minutes), we can likely meet the proposed TTFT P95 <= 300ms if we:
  * Pre-warm KV caches and pin a fraction of the model shards to favor BluePeak's pool, and
  * Allow for 10–15% elevated GPU utilization during the bursts.
- Risk: if multiple customers request similar carveouts in the same timeframe, P95 could drift and we'd need to auto-fail to a non-streaming bulk path.

Proposed operational plan:
- Redwood will create a tagged soft-pool for BluePeak for the test window, with autoscale headroom set to X+20% (we'll define X after your final RPS numbers).
- We'll instrument a short-circuit that reroutes to a non-streaming bulk endpoint if cross-tenant latency impact > 5% relative to baseline.
- Post-test: we'll provide a latency and cost report.

Next steps: Evan, send the per-minute RPS + token distribution; I'll produce a recommended token/sec ceiling and the pre-warm playbook.

Thanks — Sean
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-streaming-options.md
From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@bluepeak.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-06T10:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 load test — request for temporary streaming delivery-pattern exception

Appreciate the quick turn. Confirming:
- BluePeak agrees to the window Sept 20–24 (inclusive).
- We'll provide exact per-minute RPS and token mix by EOD Friday 8/13.
- We'll sign the one-page amendment as long as it includes: explicit rollback conditions, telemetry hooks (we need the latency/gap dashboard access during the window), and a short escalation path if we see degradation.

Evan
Evan Liu
Head of Platform, BluePeak Analytics
